hero.headline: One field. One use. No standing secret.
hero.lede: Skarbiec stores your keys, logins, sessions and tokens as per-recipient ciphertext, then hands a workload exactly the one field it signed for — once, within thirty seconds, and never again on replay.
hero.metaDescription: Skarbiec hands an agent workload exactly one credential field, once, against a signed request — and refuses the replay.

sections.heading: A read token you issued once is a token that never expires
sections.lede: Long-lived environment variables and copied credential files give every process that can read them the whole secret, for an indefinite period. An agent workload makes that boundary harder to review, not easier.

items.title: Everything reads everything
items.text: One exported variable is readable by every process in the environment, and nothing records which of them actually used it.

items.title: Nobody can answer who asked
items.text: Operators need to know which identity requested which field, reject replay, revoke access, and rotate recipients. A file on disk answers none of that.

items.title: Plaintext leaks into the trail
items.text: The moment a secret is used to debug a workload, it tends to end up in a prompt, a log line, or an audit record that outlives the incident.

sections.heading: How a workload borrows one field
sections.lede: The operator grants an exact capability, the workload proves who it is, and the capability is destroyed by its own first use. There is no step in which a standing bearer exists.

items.title: Grant one exact field
items.text: The operator registers a single `acquire:item#field` capability and an Ed25519 workload public key. Wildcards and direct capabilities cannot be mixed into that identity.

items.title: Sign the request
items.text: The workload signs the consumer, item, field, workload id, timestamp, and nonce. Skarbiec rejects stale proofs, capability mismatches, and replayed proof hashes.

items.title: Spend it once
items.text: Skarbiec issues an opaque bearer with a default 30-second TTL. The first successful matching read deletes its stored hash before returning the field.

items.title: Leave a reviewable trail
items.text: Issuance and consumption append non-sensitive identifiers to a hash-chained local journal. Secret values, one-use tokens, signatures, and public keys are excluded from it.

sections.heading: The first read succeeds. The identical retry does not.
sections.lede: This is the product's defining path, and it is executable rather than a transcript that can drift: a disposable vault, an isolated GPG keyring, and the literal non-secret value `not-a-secret`.

sections.heading: What leaves the host, in full
sections.lede: A secrets broker is worth exactly as much as its egress list. Skarbiec's is short enough to print, and the MCP surface deliberately withholds the operations that would make it longer.

sections.heading: What Skarbiec does not protect you from

items.question: Is this production-ready?
items.answer: Skarbiec is an early public `0.2.x` release, not a hosted secrets service. Deploy an exact release tag and checksum rather than inferring readiness from `Cargo.toml` or a mutable `latest` pointer.

items.question: Does it survive a compromised machine?
items.answer: No. Skarbiec does not protect secrets from a host already compromised while the matching owner key is usable, and it does not encrypt item names or other vault metadata.

items.question: What happens if the local broker cannot decrypt?
items.answer: The integration is unavailable. There is no automatic cloud fallback, because a fallback that reaches for a hosted copy would defeat the boundary the product exists to hold.

items.question: What does it cost, and what does it phone home to?
items.answer: The Apache-2.0 local core has no licence fee and no hosted dependency. No hosted control plane is required to run the CLI, MCP server, native messaging, or the HTTP broker.

items.question: Can I change the owner key later?
items.answer: `rotate-owner` rewraps every current and historical ciphertext onto the new recipient set, and the recovery recipient is preserved through owner rotation.

sections.heading: Install it and run the acquisition proof yourself
sections.lede: The quick start builds a disposable vault, spends one capability, and shows you the replay being refused. It stores nothing but the literal value `not-a-secret`, and it deletes cleanly when you are done.
